1	A cordless handheld vacuum lifter is used to move glass panes, stone slabs, and similar flat panels on site by suction gripping. A suction cup is pressed against the face of the panel, air is removed from the space enclosed between the cup and the panel, and the resulting difference between atmospheric pressure and the pressure in that enclosed space clamps the cup to the panel so that the panel can be carried.
2	
3	A suction grip is only as good as its seal. Dust on the panel, a textured or porous surface, a nick in the sealing lip, a change in temperature, or simply the slow permeation and leakage that occurs over minutes of handling will all bleed air back into the enclosed space. As air returns, the clamping force falls. The failure is progressive and, from the point of view of the person holding the panel, silent: nothing about the feel of the tool changes until the cup lets go, at which point a heavy panel is already falling.
4	
5	Vacuum lifting equipment has therefore long been fitted with vacuum monitoring. In one known lifter for transporting loads having an adhesion surface, a suction plate assembly carries projecting annular seals defining a vacuum chamber connected to a main vacuum source, a battery-fed emergency vacuum source that can be started by an emergency switch is additionally provided, and a pressure pickup associated with the vacuum chamber is coupled with a malfunction alarm such that the alarm is turned on when a preset limit pressure is exceeded during vacuum operation [REF:US-5310232-A]. That equipment is a suspended plate assembly with a main vacuum source and a separate emergency vacuum source; the alarm is described as a malfunction alarm tied to a preset limit pressure, and the reference does not describe the limit pressure in terms of the vacuum still needed to keep hold of the load.
6	
7	Control systems for vacuum lift equipment have also been described in which a programmable controller interprets feedback from vacuum level sensors and battery sensors and responsively provides warnings and limits or alters machine functions, including evaluating a change in measured vacuum level over time to determine a rate of vacuum level change that may be caused by a leak and outputting a warning indication when that rate exceeds a threshold rate [REF:US-10518985-B2]. Such a system is built around a controller with memory, stored records, and machine-function interlocks, and its leak warning is a response to how fast the vacuum is changing rather than to where the vacuum sits relative to the point at which the grip would fail.
8	
9	Powered suction devices in a hand-carried format are also known. An electric vacuum suction lifter has been described having a main body with a suction surface carrying first and second annular sealing units that bound a sealed space, a control unit, a vacuum pump controlled by the control unit to draw air from the sealed space, a pressure sensing unit that measures the pressure of the sealed space to generate instant pressure information, a battery unit that is charged by external power equipment and powers the control unit, pump, and pressure sensing unit, a start button, a pressure relief button, and at least one handle by which a member gripped by the device can be carried [REF:US-10625955-B2]. In that device the instant pressure information is compared with a high predetermined pressure and a low predetermined pressure: reaching the high predetermined pressure stops the pump, and falling below the low predetermined pressure restarts the pump. A warning unit is described as being operated when the detected battery power is below a predetermined battery power, and warning information relating to pressure is described as being transmitted to an external electronic device. A closely similar electric suction cup has likewise been described, in which the pressure detection unit detects the pressure between the suction cup and the component in real time and the vacuum pump automatically acts again when that pressure is lower than a second predetermined pressure [REF:CN-110630621-B].
10	
11	Hand-carried suction devices that signal something about their own state are also known. A sucker for plate glass has been described having a sucker body defining a suction hole at a suction surface, a manually operatable vacuum pump carried on the body, a sensor communicating with the suction channel that connects the suction hole at the suction surface with the suction hole in the pump, and a sound generator that is turned on through a switch closed by the sensor when the degree of vacuum sensed reaches a predetermined value [REF:US-5184858-A]. The pump in that device is worked by hand rather than electrically, and the sound is generated at a predetermined degree of vacuum which the reference does not relate to the vacuum still needed to retain the sheet.
12	
13	A portable hand grab has been described including one or more suction cups, at least one handle connected to the suction cups for gripping by hand, at least one electrical vacuum pump for at least partially evacuating the suction volume between the suction cups and the attachment surfaces, at least one vacuum sensor for detecting a vacuum level in the suction volume, and an electronic controller configured to control the pump to at least partially evacuate the suction volume when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being less than a preselected minimum vacuum level, optionally together with an attach indicator that the controller activates when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being greater than a preselected safe vacuum level [REF:WO-2017156581-A1]. The signal there tells the user that the vacuum is high enough to attach, and a vacuum below the preselected minimum vacuum level is answered by running the pump again rather than by telling the user that the grip is going.
14	
15	A cordless wand device for grasping objects such as silicon wafers has been described having a housing with a hollow interior, a tip attached to the housing through a hollow tube and having a perimeter region contoured to form an airtight seal against the object, a power source and a vacuum pump positioned within the housing, and light-emitting diodes of different colours which indicate to an operator whether the power source is sufficiently charged to generate sufficient suction force to safely grasp the object, that sufficiency being determined from the voltage drop across resistors connected across the power source [REF:US-5374090-A]. What is indicated in that device is the state of the power source rather than the state of the grip on the object.
16	
17	A portable electric carrying suction cup structure has been described in which a handle is fixed on the upper end of the suction cup body, a vacuum pump is provided on the suction cup body, and a control unit is connected between the power supply part and the vacuum pump, so that air continues to be pumped out after the suction cup body and the material surface have reached an airtight state; the control unit is provided with a pressure gauge by which the user can know the pressure change between the suction cup body and the surface, with a light source for displaying different usage states, and with a buzzer for sending out alarm sounds according to different usage states [REF:CN-2806399-Y]. That reference attributes the avoidance of loosening and falling during movement to the continued pumping, and it describes the buzzer as sounding according to different usage states without relating any sounding condition to the vacuum at which the cup would let go of the material.
18	
19	A digital display suction cup has been described comprising a suction cup and a handle structure, the two ends of the handle structure being provided with a switch button and a pressure relief valve, the handle structure being provided with a battery and a vacuum electric pump which is connected to the suction cup through an air pipe, with an air pressure sensor and a display screen at the lower part of the battery end, a USB charging port electrically connected to the battery, and an inner side of the suction cup provided with an evacuation hole, a pressure relief hole, and a sensing through hole [REF:US-2024424646-A1]. That device monitors and maintains negative pressure in real time and shows the negative pressure value and the battery power on the display screen as numbers for the user to read.
20	
21	Multi-cup handling equipment has been described in which two or more vacuum modules are mounted on a mounting frame, each module having a cup, an electrically powered vacuum pump, a fluid circuit, a controller, and optionally a pressure sensor and a battery, with an interface through which a user selects an operational mode of the modules, and in which each module may include indicators that indicate a functional condition of the module visually or audibly [REF:WO-2022236379-A1].
22	
23	Three shortcomings persist for a person who is holding a panel in one hand. First, the response to a decaying grip in the known powered devices is to run the pump again: the device treats a falling vacuum as a housekeeping event to be corrected, and the low pressure value at which it acts is chosen with reference to the working vacuum, not with reference to how much grip is left. If the leak is larger than the pump can make up - a torn lip, a dusty or porous panel, a cracked substrate - the pump simply runs while the grip continues to decay, and the user is told nothing until the panel is gone. Second, where a signal is given, it is given on a condition unrelated to grip (battery state), on a rate of change, on a preset limit whose relationship to the load-holding capacity of the cup is not established, as a confirmation that the vacuum is high enough to attach, or as a number on a display which the user must look at and interpret while carrying a panel. None of these delivers the one thing a person carrying a slab actually needs: notice that arrives while the cup is still holding, with grip left over to get the panel down.
24	
25	Third, the equipment that has the most elaborate response to a failing grip is the equipment that is not carried in the hand. A suspended plate assembly can be provided with a battery-fed emergency vacuum source that an emergency switch starts [REF:US-5310232-A], and a controller for vacuum lift equipment can limit or alter machine functions in response to sensor feedback [REF:US-10518985-B2]. A lifter that is carried in the hand has none of those remedies available to it: the only thing that can act on a failing grip is the person holding the handle, and that person can only act if the notice arrives early enough.
26	
27	There remains a need for a cordless handheld vacuum lifter that tells the user that the grip is failing while the cup is still holding, so that the warning arrives before the load can be dropped.

findings.detail: The draft asserts twice that the US-5310232-A lifter is suspended, and builds its third stated shortcoming on the premise that this reference (with US-10518985-B2) is equipment "that is not carried in the hand". prior_art/US-5310232-A.md contains no word about suspension, hanging, a crane, a hoist, or how the lifter is supported, and no statement that it is not hand-carried; a keyword search of that file for "suspend", "crane", "hoist", "hand", "portable" and "carr" returns no matches. The reference's own claim language calls the element "a suction plate assembly", not a suspended one. The unsupported adjective is not decorative: the paragraph at line 25 uses the not-hand-carried premise as the reason the reference's remedies are unavailable to the claimed lifter.
findings.evidence: Draft (line 5): "That equipment is a suspended plate assembly with a main vacuum source and a separate emergency vacuum source; the alarm is described as a malfunction alarm tied to a preset limit pressure..." Draft (line 25): "Third, the equipment that has the most elaborate response to a failing grip is the equipment that is not carried in the hand. A suspended plate assembly can be provided with a battery-fed emergency vacuum source that an emergency switch starts [REF:US-5310232-A]..." Source (prior_art/US-5310232-A.md, Claims): "A vacuum lifter, comprising: a) a suction plate assembly; b) at least first and second seals projecting from sid assembly and defining therebetween a vacuum chamber..." Source (Abstract): "The invention concerns a vacuum lifter to transport loads with an adhesion surface and comprises at least one suction head with at least one projecting annular seal on its suction side..."
findings.fix: In line 5 replace "That equipment is a suspended plate assembly" with "That equipment is a suction plate assembly". Recast the opening of line 25 to assert only what the two files support, e.g.: "Third, the remedies that the known equipment brings to a failing grip are remedies a cordless hand tool does not have. A suction plate assembly can be provided with a battery-fed emergency vacuum source that an emergency switch starts [REF:US-5310232-A], and a controller for vacuum lift equipment can limit or alter machine functions in response to sensor feedback [REF:US-10518985-B2]. A lifter that is carried in the hand has none of those remedies available to it: the only thing that can act on a failing grip is the person holding the handle, and that person can only act if the notice arrives early enough."

findings.title: US-5374090-A described as indicating power-source state "rather than the state of the grip", contrary to the indicating-means language in its own claims
findings.where: draft/05-background.md, paragraph beginning "A cordless wand device for grasping objects..." (line 15), and the list of signalling conditions in the paragraph beginning "Three shortcomings persist..." (line 23)
findings.detail: The draft's concluding characterisation of US-5374090-A, and the corresponding entry "(battery state)" in the shortcomings list, state that the reference's indication is unrelated to the grip. The reference file recites the indicating means, in both independent claims, as means for indicating whether the suction force is of sufficient strength to grasp the object, with one LED illuminating when the suction force is sufficient to grasp and another when it is not. The draft's earlier sentence accurately reports the abstract's power-source framing and the resistor-based determination; it is the added conclusion that the indication is of "the state of the power source rather than the state of the grip on the object" that the file does not support and that its claim text cuts against. The honest and equally usable point - that sufficiency is inferred from voltage drop across resistors rather than from a measured vacuum - is already in the draft's own preceding clause.
findings.evidence: Draft (line 15): "What is indicated in that device is the state of the power source rather than the state of the grip on the object." Draft (line 23): "Second, where a signal is given, it is given on a condition unrelated to grip (battery state), on a rate of change, on a preset limit..." Source (prior_art/US-5374090-A.md, Claims): "means for indicating to an operator whether said suction force is of sufficient strength to grasp said object, said indicating means comprising: a first light-emitting diode which illuminates when said means for creating a suction force is activated and said suction force is of sufficient strength to grasp said object; a second light-emitting diode which illuminates when said means for creating a suction force is activated and said suction force is not of sufficient strength to grasp said object; and means for determining the sufficiency of said suction force."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence at line 15 with: "The sufficiency that is indicated in that device is determined from the charge state of the power source rather than from a measured vacuum in the grip." In the list at line 23, replace "on a condition unrelated to grip (battery state)" with "on the charge state of the power source rather than on a measured vacuum".

findings.title: Threshold-selection rationale generalised to "the known powered devices" when only one cited file states any such relationship
findings.where: draft/05-background.md, paragraph beginning "Three shortcomings persist..." (line 23), first shortcoming
findings.detail: The draft states of the known powered devices generally that the low pressure value at which the pump restarts "is chosen with reference to the working vacuum". That is supported for US-10625955-B2, whose claim 1 fixes the low predetermined pressure relative to the high predetermined pressure at which the pump stops. It is not stated in the files for WO-2017156581-A1 (which recites only "a preselected minimum vacuum level", with no account of how it is selected) or CN-110630621-B ("a second preset pressure", likewise unexplained). The negative half of the sentence - that none of them relates the value to how much grip is left - is accurate for all three; only the positive attribution over-reaches. I am flagging this as minor because the sentence is a summarising passage carrying no [REF:] tag, but it is stated as fact about the cited art.
findings.evidence: Draft (line 23): "...the device treats a falling vacuum as a housekeeping event to be corrected, and the low pressure value at which it acts is chosen with reference to the working vacuum, not with reference to how much grip is left." Source (prior_art/US-10625955-B2.md, claim 1): "wherein a negative pressure value corresponding to the high predetermined pressure is greater than a negative pressure value corresponding to the low predetermined pressure." Source (prior_art/WO-2017156581-A1.md, claim 1): "...to at least partially evacuate the suction volume when the vacuum sensor detects the vacuum level being less than a preselected minimum vacuum level." Source (prior_art/CN-110630621-B.md, Abstract): "When the pressure sensing unit detects that the pressure between the electric suction cup and the component is lower than a second preset pressure, the vacuum pump automatically acts to pump out the air..."
findings.fix: Narrow the clause to what the files say, e.g.: "...and where the relationship of that low pressure value is stated at all, it is stated relative to the working vacuum at which the pump stops [REF:US-10625955-B2]; none of these references relates it to how much grip is left."

data.summary: The specification body, claims, numerals and figure briefs are internally consistent and faithful to the inventor's disclosure: all 16 numerals label one part each across the description, numerals.md and the three figure briefs; the Brief Description matches what each brief shows; and every claim limitation (including the method claim 5 steps) traces to the disclosure's own words and to the detailed description. No unsupported structure, material, dimension, threshold or embodiment was added. Pixel verification was impossible because figures/ contains no rendered-*.png files and review/figure-audit-evidence.json is absent from the workspace; that absence is what the two already-reported mechanical checks describe, so it is not re-reported as a finding. The defects found are in the Background's handling of two cited references: US-5310232-A is twice called a "suspended" plate assembly, a fact its file never states and which carries the whole third-shortcoming argument, and US-5374090-A is said to indicate only power-source state when its own claims recite indicating whether the suction force is sufficient to grasp the object. A third, minor over-generalisation attributes a threshold-selection rationale to "the known powered devices" that only one reference actually states.
